sentences.text: Lusitanisuchus belongs to the class Reptilia and falls within the parent group Mesoeucrocodylia.

The single species, Lusitanisuchus mitracostatus, was named in 2004 after earlier being described as Lisboasaurus in 1970. A later reexamination of fossils from the Guimarota Formation found skull material, including a dentary similar to the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — proving it was a crocodylomorph rather than a lizard.
Lusitanisuchus coexisted with many dinosaurs in the Lusitanian Basin during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.

Teeth found at Porto Dinheiro, Lourinhã in Berriasian strata extend the known temporal range of the taxon by about 15 million years. The genus lived from 152.21 to 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage.
